blocks.text: I can understand descriptions of personal future plans using verbs in the simple future and in the conditional with ‘vouloir’.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: a form of future that describes what will happen
a form of verb that describes what would happen

blocks.text: The 1-verb future translates what **will** happen. It is the equivalent of ‘will’ + verb, and it is formed with **one word**. Its name in French is ‘le futur simple’.

blocks.label: Where is the word ‘will’?
blocks.text: There is no separate word for ‘will’ in French. The spelling of the verb carries the whole meaning.
For predictable -er verbs, use the infinitive and add {-ai}, {-as}, {-a}. Tap a row to build the word.
The endings are the same as present tense ‘avoir’. That is a useful memory hook!

blocks.q: Which sentence is in the 1-verb future?
blocks.why: étudiera is the infinitive étudier + -a, so it means ‘he will study’. There is no separate word for ‘will’: the ending does the job.

blocks.q: Choose the correct 1-verb future form. The English clue tells you who is speaking.

items.q: Je ___ avec mon copain. (parler: I will speak)
Tu ___ au foot. (jouer: you will play)
Elle ___ une ile française. (visiter: she will visit)
Il ___ son apprentissage. (commencer: he will start)

blocks.q: Match each 1-verb future form to its English meaning.

blocks.text: The conditional says what **would** happen. ‘Vouloir’ in the conditional means **would like**, so it is useful for expressing a wish. Here are the singular forms.
The singular endings all sound the same!
Conditional ‘vouloir’ can be followed by an **infinitive** verb or by a **noun**.

items: Il voudrait visiter Paris = He would like to visit Paris (infinitive).
Ma mère voudrait me rendre visite = My mother would like to visit me (infinitive).
Je voudrais un cadeau = I would like a present (noun).
Je voudrais une carte pour ma grand-mère = I would like a card for my grandmother (noun).

blocks.q: Choose the correct form of conditional ‘vouloir’. Look at who is speaking.

items.q: Tu ___ un chien. (you would like a dog)
Mon copain ___ visiter Paris. (my friend would like to visit Paris)
Je ___ un cheval. (I would like a horse)
Elle ___ un lapin. (she would like a rabbit)

blocks.text: The 1-verb future means ‘will’ + verb. The conditional means ‘would’ + verb. Both are **simple** forms: all the meaning is contained in a single word.

blocks.label: Is there a French word for ‘would’?
blocks.text: No. There is no separate word for ‘will’ or ‘would’ in French. Look at the verb’s ending to tell which one you have: je parlerai means ‘I will speak’ and je voudrais means ‘I would like’.

blocks.q: Is each verb in the 1-verb future (will) or the conditional (would)?

items.text: Je voudrais un lapin et deux chats
Un jour, je visiterai toutes les capitales
Tu voudrais faire un voyage en Afrique

blocks.q: Match the new words to their meanings.

blocks.label: Friends in French
blocks.text: ‘Un copain’ and ‘une copine’ mean a friend. They can also mean a boyfriend or girlfriend.
Léa says: ‘Après nos vacances en Corse, je commencerai mon apprentissage en informatique.’

blocks.q: How can you tell that Léa is talking about the future?
options: The verb commencerai is the infinitive commencer + -ai
There is a separate word for ‘will’ in the sentence
blocks.why: commencer + -ai gives je commencerai. The ending carries the meaning ‘will’, and the ending is -ai, not -ais.

items: The 1-verb future translates ‘will’ + verb. It is formed with one word.
For -er verbs, add {-ai}, {-as}, {-a} to the infinitive: je parlerai, tu parleras, il/elle/on parlera.
Conditional ‘vouloir’ expresses a wish (would like). It can be followed by a noun or an infinitive.
The singular forms sound the same: je voudrais, tu voudrais, il/elle/on voudrait.

flashcards.back: What will happen. It is the equivalent of ‘will’ + verb and it is formed with one word.

flashcards.front: What is the French name for the 1-verb future?
How do you form the 1-verb future of a predictable -er verb for je, tu, il/elle/on?
flashcards.back:
Add -ai, -as, -a to the infinitive.

parler → je parlerai, tu parleras, il/elle/on parlera

flashcards.front: Which verb’s present-tense forms are the same as the 1-verb future endings -ai, -as, -a?
flashcards.back: avoir. That is a useful memory hook.

flashcards.front: Say ‘I will speak’ in French (1-verb future of parler).
Is there a separate French word for ‘will’?
flashcards.back: No. The spelling of the verb carries the whole meaning.

flashcards.front: What does ‘vouloir’ in the conditional mean, and what is it useful for?
flashcards.back: It means ‘would like’. It is useful for expressing a wish.

flashcards.front: Give the singular conditional forms of ‘vouloir’.
flashcards.back: je voudrais, tu voudrais, il/elle voudrait, on voudrait

flashcards.front: What can conditional ‘vouloir’ be followed by?
flashcards.back:
A noun or an infinitive.

Je voudrais un cadeau. Il voudrait visiter Paris.

flashcards.front: Do the singular forms of conditional ‘vouloir’ sound different from each other?
flashcards.back: No. Je voudrais, tu voudrais and il/elle voudrait all sound the same.

flashcards.front: Put ‘On étudie beaucoup’ (we are studying a lot) into the 1-verb future.
flashcards.back: On étudiera beaucoup. (We will study a lot.)

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Futurs divers : future -er verbs (singular), conditional ‘vouloir’ (singular)
worksheet.instructions: Write your answers in French unless the question asks for English. Include the pronoun when the question shows one, and check your accents.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the 1-verb future of parler: ‘I will speak’.
Write in French, using the 1-verb future of étudier and the pronoun on: ‘we will study’.
questions.explanation: For on, add -a to the infinitive: étudier + -a = on étudiera.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the 1-verb future of rêver: ‘you (singular) will dream’.
questions.explanation: For tu, add -as to the infinitive: rêver + -as = tu rêveras.

questions.prompt: Which ending do you add to the infinitive of a predictable -er verb to make the 1-verb future for tu? Write the ending only.
questions.explanation: The singular endings are -ai, -as, -a: tu takes -as.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with the conditional of vouloir: Je ______ une carte pour ma grand-mère. (I would like a card for my grandmother.)
questions.explanation: With je, conditional ‘vouloir’ is je voudrais, and it can be followed by a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with the conditional of vouloir: Ma mère ______ me rendre visite. (My mother would like to visit me.)
questions.explanation: With il, elle (and ma mère), conditional ‘vouloir’ is voudrait.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of vouloir: ‘He would like to visit Paris.’
‘On mangera au restaurant.’ Is the verb in the 1-verb future or the conditional? Answer with one word: future or conditional.
questions.explanation: mangera is the infinitive manger + -a, so it means ‘will eat’.

questions.prompt: ‘Tu voudrais faire un voyage en Afrique.’ Is the verb in the 1-verb future or the conditional? Answer with one word: future or conditional.
What does ‘même si’ mean in English?
Write in French: ‘a rabbit’ (include the word for ‘a’).
